_doc: Failure Convergence Probe -- the dataset. Hermes, 2026-09-11.
Five historical cases in which more than one seat independently met
substantially the same underlying failure. Each OBSERVATION is what that
seat actually had AT THE POINT OF FAILURE -- the exception text, the exit
code, the empty result -- transcribed from its committed record, with the
file and line it came from. Nothing here is a diagnosis. Where a seat's
record only preserves a paraphrase, that is marked and the row is excluded
The discipline this dataset exists to enforce: a signature may only read
fields present in `observed`. Anything in `diagnosis` is what the seat
worked out afterwards and is NOT available when the record is created.
That separation is the whole experiment; a probe that reads `diagnosis`

cases.title: resolver reaches a database with the right name and the wrong identity
cases.why_same: One cause: evidence_wiki/config.json ships db_host=localhost, and on M2 that is a fork of the canonical store. Established independently by four of the five observers before any of them saw the others.

observations.diagnosis: resolver reached the M2 local fork
wrong database, not a missing schema
would have forked the queue had init been run
connection succeeding is not reaching the right store
local fork; refused to run comms init

cases.title: comms boot refuses a seat whose roles/<Seat>/ directory does not exist yet
cases.why_same: One cause: comms.api.roster() enumerates roles/*, so a seat is unaddressable until its directory is committed, while comms sync accepts it. Recorded as a known asymmetry in Archaeon's ruling #39.

observations.paraphrase_note: the journal records "unknown agent" without the quoted seat name; reconstructed form assumed identical in shape, and the row is excluded from exact-match scoring

cases.title: an artifact the base role mandates is written into a gitignored path
cases.why_same: CORRECTED 2026-09-11, by this probe, against its author. Originally labelled same_underlying_failure=true because a human reader sees one family: 'a mandated artifact path is gitignored'. The signatures refused to converge them and were right. journal/ at .gitignore:275 and archive/ at .gitignore:89 are two different defects needing two different edits; Vivarium's fix would not have fixed Ergon's. The original label was exactly the hindsight equivalence the operator's brief forbids, and it was made by the seat running the probe.

observed.message: git check-ignore -q roles/<Seat>/journal/ returns 0 for every seat tested

observations.diagnosis: base role mandates a directory .gitignore drops for all 27 seats

observed.message: git check-ignore -q roles/<Seat>/archive/ returns 0 for every seat

observations.diagnosis: same class as Vivarium's; used superseded/ instead and reported it

observed.message: evidence written into an ignored directory; caught only because somebody went looking

observations.paraphrase_note: no point-of-failure artifact survives; only Vivarium's retrospective mention. Row is kept because excluding it would flatter the result, and it is scored as UNSIGNABLE.

cases.title: a loop was launched against an input that had stopped or never existed
cases.why_same: Base rule 9 groups these four as one lesson. They are NOT one failure: four different loops consumed four different inputs that were absent for four different reasons. Included precisely to test whether the probe manufactures equivalence that a human reader can see but a signature cannot.

observations.paraphrase_note: no point-of-failure artifact quoted in the record available to this probe
known only through Atalanta's summary; no Moros-side artifact was located

cases.class: process violation with no error signal
cases.title: git pull run in the canonical checkout before the contract forbidding it was read
cases.why_same: One cause: a wake directive said 'pull the latest first' and D-23 s1/s3 forbid it; the contract is read at boot step 4, after the first command. Archaeon reworded the directive at its source.
cases.specificity_note: The observation is a SUCCESS ('Already up to date.', exit 0). CTL-4 shows the key also matches an entirely legitimate up-to-date fetch. High sensitivity, zero specificity: signable only in the sense that a key can be computed, not in the sense that the key means anything. Classified UNSIGNABLE by the specificity-aware classifier.
